figures.before: What You're Actually Deciding: Is the Problem Fixable Without Tearing Down?
figures.alt: Selective interior demolition in an existing building with protected structure, organized debris removal, and retained areas clearly separated
figures.caption: The renovation-versus-rebuild decision starts with the real existing condition. Structure, foundation, envelope, systems, layout, permits, site constraints, cost, time, and the work needed to make the result durable all matter.

figures.before: When the Foundation Forces the Decision: Slab Failures, Settling, Termite Damage
figures.alt: Coastal home elevated foundation with reinforced concrete piers, structural beams, and open site access below the floor framing
figures.caption: A foundation problem needs diagnosis before the decision is made. The underlying support, soils, water, load path, repair access, future risk, and effect on the rest of the house can change the viable options.

figures.before: Historic Designation: Renovation May Be Required to Maintain Historic Registry Status
figures.alt: Historic wood window sill under careful repair with sound retained material, matching wood pieces, and protected surrounding trim
figures.caption: Historic properties add another layer to the decision. Repair, replacement, materials, visible exterior work, approvals, sequencing, and the preservation of significant features need to be considered before committing to a path.
